• There is a growing imbalance between the rate of structure determinations and the rate of publications.
In summary, our research is concerned with

1. the development of new methods for data acquisition and analysis, 2. the development of methods for the efficient publication of structural results, 3. the dissemination of crystallographic information, and 4. the development of a new generation of software tools for the analysis and visualisation of structural data.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crystallographic community has a moral responsibility to publish, and to make available, as many of its structures as possible.
the current situation is unsatisfactory, and that it is in the interests of the community that it is resolved.
the crystallographic community is currently in a state of flux, and that there is a great deal of work still to be done to achieve a satisfactory and sustainable situation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crystallographic databases and journals are not yet doing enough to ensure the public availability of crystal structure data.
we have a problem with data access, but we do not yet have a solution.
we are now in the position to be able to determine structures at a rate that is limited by the time required for the deposition, publication and archiving of the results.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to develop new ways of working with crystal structures, and to develop a new ‘culture’ of crystal structure data management.

there are many opportunities for crystallography to make a major contribution towards the development of the next generation of scientific databases, and that this will require a new generation of crystallographers who are able to work with the new technologies and who are willing to take the necessary steps in the right direction.

crystallographers should not be the only ones who are concerned with this problem, but should be working in concert with the journals and the crystallographic databases to maximise public data availability.
